resources.string: The text and the background cannot be the same colour.
The background colour shows wherever no image does.
Landscape — the time’s share of the width: %1$d%%
Portrait — the time’s share of the height: %1$d%%
Everything sizes itself to fill its share, until it would not fit.
Image — tap a name to rename
BG puts an image behind the clock; Text shows it inside the digits. An image serves one or the other — ticking one clears the other — and with neither it is held: kept, used nowhere.
No images yet; the clock is white on plain black.
A name like “001 sunrise.jpg” sorts wherever you put the number.
That name is already used by another image.
PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or BMP. Each show plays its images in the order listed here. An animated GIF plays through once, however long that is; a still image holds for the time above.
That file is not an image this device can read.

Add a font from a file\u2026
TrueType (.ttf), OpenType (.otf) or a collection (.ttc). Anything this device cannot read as a font is refused.

reteclock is not your screensaver yet.
Opens Android\'s own screensaver settings — it hides in a different place on every version. Pick reteclock there, and choose when it should come on (while charging, or in a dock).
This phone has no screensaver settings screen.
Press and hold the clock for settings
Started without images or imported fonts: the last run stopped answering. Press and hold for settings.
Home-screen button opens the clock directly
Off, the button opens this screen — the way back in when an image or a font has made the clock unusable. A run that stopped answering opens this screen either way.
The last run stopped answering, so the clock started without images or imported fonts. A large animated GIF is the usual reason: remove it below, or untick BG, and start the clock again.
